##: TEMPLATE, not the manifest users install. `make deploy-scoop` renders it with
scripts/render-package-manifest.mjs from the release's verified artifact-manifest.json
and commits the result to flowreader-app/scoop-bucket as bucket/flowreader.json. The
MSI is downloaded through the download counter (get.flowreader.io/r/, infra/download-worker),
which counts the install and redirects to the public release repository
flowreader-app/flowreader. The `#/<file>.msi` fragment names the downloaded file for
Scoop (it is never sent to the server); without it the query string would. 1.1.5 and
dfb050667e6ef3791f0b460e9d8041ecac8371d33a507f3eb94f14177c33236a come from that manifest, the same record the delivery gate checks
THE MSI IS UNSIGNED. The project holds no Authenticode certificate, so build-windows.yml
(packaging/release-repo/) records the windows artifact as signatureStatus: unsigned. Scoop itself does not care
-- it verifies the download by SHA-256, which is what `hash` below is -- but Windows
does: SmartScreen shows an 'unrecognized app' prompt the first time flowreader.exe
runs. The `notes` field says so to the user at install time.
`extract_dir`: Scoop extracts an .msi with msiexec /a (or lessmsi) into SourceDir, and
the Tauri/WiX admin image puts the payload under PFiles\FlowReader (ProgramFiles64Folder
is PFiles in an admin image). Check with `msiextract -l <msi>` (Homebrew msitools): it
lists PFiles/FlowReader/flowreader.exe. 1.0.0 shipped with `FlowReader` here and failed
description: Read faster while maintaining comprehension. A distraction-free reading app with pacing aids.
notes: FlowReader's installer is not code-signed: the project holds no Authenticode certificate.
Windows SmartScreen will show an 'unrecognized app' warning the first time you run it.
Choose 'More info' then 'Run anyway'. Scoop has already verified the download against
the SHA-256 listed in the release's SHA256SUMS.txt.
